- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment includes multiple 0.0 values (especially consecutive), model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast slightly to compensate for lagged sentiment signals.
- After a recent spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently overcorrects with a sharp downward forecast; cap downward movement to avoid overshoot.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d forecast with 1st few days showing high volatility), model often underestimates downward trend; apply slight upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows a recent shift from positive to neutral/negative, model tends to lag in adjusting downward; apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
